draft_key_information_units.information: Profit before tax decreased to ISK 1,545 million in Q2 2026 from ISK 2,025 million in Q2 2025, a 23.7% year-over-year decline, primarily due to lower net fee income and one-off efficiency measure costs.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Profit before tax ISK 1,545 m. compared to ISK 2,025 m. in Q2 2025 Decreasing by ISK 480 m. from previous year, or 23.7%. Administrative expenses ISK 2,947 m., decreasing by 1.1% YoY despite one-off costs of ISK 112 m. in the quarter attributable to cost efficiency measures in June.

draft_key_information_units.information: Net interest income increased to ISK 3,013 million in Q2 2026 from ISK 2,962 million in Q2 2025, a 1.7% year-over-year increase, driven by loan book growth partially offset by the ISK 10.2 billion dividend payment impact and lower inflation.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Net interest income ISK 3,013 m. compared to ISK 2,962 m. in Q2 2025 Increasing by ISK 51 m. from previous year or 1.7%. Net interest income decreased by ISK 253 m. from Q1 2026, mainly due to lower inflation in Q2 affecting Kvika's positive inflation balance of ISK 6.1 bn., as well as the impact of the ISK 10.2 bn. dividend payment in June.

draft_key_information_units.information: Net fee and commission income decreased significantly to ISK 1,416 million in Q2 2026 from ISK 1,935 million in Q2 2025, a 26.8% year-over-year decline, reflecting subdued market activity across all business lines.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Net fee and commission income ISK 1,416 m. compared to ISK 1,935 m. in Q2 2025 Decreasing by ISK 519 m. from previous year or 26.8%. Activity in capital markets remained subdued during the quarter, with lower transaction volumes and softer client activity weighing on fee generation across all business lines.

draft_key_information_units.information: Balance sheet expanded with loans to customers increasing to ISK 223.3 billion at end-Q2 2026 (7.6% from year-end 2025) and deposits surging to ISK 201.2 billion (16.5% from year-end 2025), while total assets grew to ISK 375.7 billion (9.5% from year-end 2025).
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Loans to customers amounted to ISK 223.3 bn. at the end of Q2 2026, increasing by ISK 15.8 bn., or 7.6%, from year-end 2025. Deposits amounted to ISK 201.2 bn. at the end of Q2 2026, increasing by 16.5% from year-end 2025. Total assets amounted to ISK 375.7 bn. at the end of Q2 2026, increasing by 9.5% from year-end 2025.

draft_key_information_units.information: Capital adequacy ratio (CAR) stood at 23.0% at end-Q2 2026, down from 26.8% at year-end 2025 primarily due to the ISK 10.2 billion dividend distribution in June, while remaining well above regulatory requirements.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: CAR of 23.0% at 30 June 2026, decreasing as special dividend was distributed in June. CAR above regulatory capital requirements 200-400 bps. management buffer ~~✓~~ 530 bps. Following the 2026 SREP results received on 30 June 2026, Kvika's Pillar II requirement reduced by 0.2%, lowering the Bank's total capital requirement to 17.7%. The bank continues to target a management buffer of 2% to 4% over current and anticipated CAR requirements.

draft_key_information_units.information: Liquidity coverage ratio (LCR) remained strong at 276% at end-Q2 2026, well above the 100% regulatory requirement, supported by high-quality liquid assets of ISK 76.4 billion (81% Level 1 assets).
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: The liquidity coverage ratio (LCR) remains strong at 276%, well above the 100% regulatory requirement. High-quality liquid assets (HQLA) amounted to ISK 76.4 bn., of which 81% were classified as Level 1 assets.

draft_key_information_units.information: Major strategic developments include: (1) Efficiency measures announced in June expected to achieve annualized cost savings of ISK 300-400 million; (2) Ongoing divestment of Straumur greiðslumiðlun hf. expected to close before year-end; (3) CEO Ármann Þorvaldsson to step down by year-end 2026 after nearly ten years with the Group.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Efficiency measures announced in June expected to achieve annualised cost savings of ISK 300-400 m. Sale of Straumur greiðslumiðlun hf. in progress. Due diligence underway following a formal sales process. CEO Ármann Þorvaldsson to step down by year-end 2026. Ármann has requested to step down from his position after nearly ten years with the Group.

draft_key_information_units.information: Segment highlights: Commercial Banking showed strong deposit and loan growth; Investment Banking delivered robust lending despite challenging markets; Asset Management onboarded a new institutional investor; UK business maintained strong deal momentum with loan book at all-time high.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Commercial Banking: Strong deposit growth (ISK 12 bn.), loan book growth (ISK 6 bn.). Investment Banking: Loan book grew by nearly 4% qoq. Asset Management: New institutional investor onboarded (ISK 5 bn. AUM). UK: Loan book reached all-time high, strong pipeline converted, Harpa PE investments increased to six.

draft_key_information_units.information: Credit quality remains strong with impairment levels stable at 1.2% of gross loan book, supported by well-collateralized Stage 3 exposures (average LTV 52.2%) and no broader portfolio deterioration despite macroeconomic challenges.
draft_key_information_units.source_evidence: Credit quality remains strong, with no signs of broader deterioration despite a prolonged period of elevated interest rates and inflation. Overall impairment levels remain low and stable at 1.2% of the gross loan book. Stage 3 loans remain well-collateralised, with an average loan-to-value of 52.2%, supporting the overall low credit risk profile.

evaluation.selection_rationale: Selected 9 units covering all prioritized material areas: headline profitability (D1), key income drivers (D2-D3), balance sheet growth (D4), capital position (D5), liquidity (D6), major strategic developments (D7), and segment performance highlights (D8) plus credit quality (D9). Units are independently omittable themes without duplication. All factual details are directly supportable by the source report. REFERENCE SUMMARY was used to validate salience of profit metrics, balance sheet figures, and period-over-period changes, but units extend beyond reference to include strategic developments and credit quality which are material but not exhaustively covered in the reference. Omitted routine boilerplate such as governance, remuneration, risk lists, accounting policies, and minor technical details per instructions.
